headline: Pangenome graphs and genome benchmarks advance bacterial resistance and typing analysis
label: Pangenome Graphs And Resistance Genomics
summary: Recent preprints and papers apply pangenome and assembly graphs to resistance genes, typing, and taxonomy across bacterial genomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the move from single linear references toward pangenome and assembly graph representations for bacterial and metagenomic analysis. Panomap maps raw nanopore signals to pangenome variation graphs, reducing reference bias and scaling sublinearly with collection size, while PANORAMA applies rule-based prediction and cross-species comparison over pangenome graphs. Sarand extracts resistance gene neighbourhoods directly from metagenomic assembly graphs, and the long-read methylation study links resistance genes to wastewater bacterial hosts and genetic contexts. amR packages BV-BRC genomes, pangenome features and interpretable ML for resistance prediction. Other items address validation rather than representation: a benchmark across 30,495 type-strain genomes finds no single method optimal at all taxonomic ranks, CurateMake provides auditable ITS reference harmonisation with phylogenetic validation, and a high-resolution core genome MLST and LIN scheme targets S. pyogenes outbreak detection.
